Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

consist in verb

also lie in, be a matter of, it all comes down to, it’s all about

classical

Cic. Rep. 1.2: virtūs in ūsū suī tōta posita est (Lewis & Short)

positum esse in

phrase: perfect participle of pōnō with esse, and in with the ablative

lie in, consist in, rest on

Literally “be placed in”. It also means “depend on”: in tē positum est, it is up to you (Lewis & Short s.v. pōnō). Cicero also says locātum esse in (Off. 3.71).

Other words

  • in eō est, ut — it consists in this, that; it all comes down to

    phrase, with ut and the subjunctive · also used · classical · Cic. Q. Fr. 3.1.1: tōtum in eō est tectōrium, ut sit concinnum (Lewis & Short s.v. in)

    Lewis & Short: “it consists in that, depends upon that”. With a subject of time it means instead “be on the point of” (in eō erat, ut).

Examples

  • virtūs in ūsū suī tōta posita est

    virtue consists entirely in its useCic. Rep. 1.2 (Lewis & Short)

  • tōtum in eō est tectōrium, ut sit concinnum

    with plasterwork, it all comes down to its being neatCic. Q. Fr. 3.1.1 (Lewis & Short)

  • prūdentia est locāta in dēlēctū bonōrum et malōrum

    good sense consists in choosing between good and badCic. Off. 3.71 (Lewis & Short)

See also consist of, involve, depend.

Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, with its references, in the house spelling (macrons, consonantal j); they have not been checked against a modern edition.
